checks.label: The polynomial factor theorem: if P(x) has a root x = a, i.e. if P(a) = 0, then x − a is a factor of P(x). For every screen's rule and every handle setting, at every whole a from −6 to 6, dividing by (x − a) leaves exactly P(a) over, so it leaves 0 exactly where P(a) = 0

Dividing x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 by (x − 4) gives x² − 2x + 3 with 6 left, and P(4) = 64 − 96 + 44 − 6 = 6; by (x − 1) it gives x² − 5x + 6 with 0 left; the remainders for a = −1 to 5 are −24, −6, 0, 0, 0, 6 and 24; by (x − 5) it leaves 24, and by (x + 5) −336

Each handle puts its bracket in the rule: 1, 2, 3 give (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3) = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6; −1, 2, 4 give x³ − 5x² + 2x + 8; 1, 2, 2 give (x − 1)(x − 2)² = x³ − 5x² + 8x − 4; 2, 2, 2 give (x − 2)³ = x³ − 6x² + 12x − 8; −1, 3, 3 give (x + 1)(x − 3)² = x³ − 5x² + 3x + 9; and at every setting the rule is 0 at each handle and the rows say so
A root that comes twice touches: near it the curve stays on one side of the axis; once or three times it crosses, and three times it flattens there (its slope is 0)

Every puzzle accepts only its right answer, and each wrong pick fails where the lesson says: 1 × 4 × 6 = 24 and −2 × −3 × −5 = −30; P(−2) = 12 and P(6) = 180 for x³ − 7x + 6; P(5) = 24 and P(−5) = −336; P(−1) = 8 and P(2) = −4 for x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6; P(1) = 0 for x³ − 3x + 2; each right rule multiplies back to the question's

The worked numbers: 504 ÷ 9 = 56, and at x = 10 the division is the same sum (1000 − 600 + 110 − 6 = 504, 10 − 1 = 9, 100 − 50 + 6 = 56); x³ + 8 gives 9, 7, 16 and 0 at 1, −1, 2 and −2 and leaves x² − 2x + 4, whose discriminant is 4 − 16 = −12; the slip gives x² − 7x + 4 with −2 left and expands back to x³ − 8x² + 11x − 6; the look ahead gives A = 2, B = 3, and −0.5 on both sides at x = 0

To factorise the quadratic x² + bx + c, the sum of the two numbers in the brackets must be b, and the product must be c: each quadratic left once a bracket splits off has two such numbers, and they are the rule's other roots with their signs swapped

The picture follows the rule: on each screen with the try marker, at every whole setting, the dot sits on the axis exactly where P(a) reads 0, and only there does a handle appear and the bracket (x − a) split off, leaving a quadratic that multiplies back to the rule; on the remainder screen the row is (x − a) times what comes out, plus P(a)
Before Check each puzzle keeps its answer back (no bracket form, curve or handles that give it away), and after a right answer shows it whole, with the marker ending on the value asked for
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
